info.home.title: Home — turning on and strategy
info.home:
Press “Turn on”: in most networks that is enough — the app picks a strategy by itself. Change it only if sites stop opening.

This is where connection optimization is turned on for this computer. “Turn on” starts it; if no strategy is chosen yet, the app first picks one — usually within a few minutes. If sites still do not open after that, press “Find strategy” (the “Strategy” tab). With the service (“Install service” right here or “Settings” → “Service mode”) it works without the window and usually starts by itself after a reboot (if not, the reason is usually shown in “Diagnostics”); without the service — only while the app is open (window or icon next to the clock). A strategy is a set of techniques the app uses to adapt the connection to the provider's equipment; different providers need different ones. Changing the strategy restarts optimization — open connections drop for a second.
info.select.title: Strategy search — quick / full / deep
info.select:
Run it if sites stopped opening: “Full” is more reliable, “Quick” is faster.

The search goes through strategies and checks whether YouTube, Discord and your addresses open. “Quick” stops at the first one where everything opened — usually a few minutes. “Full” checks all of them and picks the most reliable. If none opens everything, and YouTube, Discord and your sites each prefer a different one, the app combines them into a “Mixed” strategy, checks it and turns it on when it beats the single ones. If the ready-made strategies did not help, the result offers “Search deeper” — the app generates new strategies, usually up to 15 minutes. During the search optimization is turned on and off several times — sites and games will be interrupted. The search turns on the best strategy by itself; another one can be selected in the table with “Apply selected”.
info.sites.title: Sites — your own and excluded
info.sites:
Add a site if it does not open while YouTube and Discord work.

This is where sites that should open besides YouTube and Discord are added: for example, example.com or a full link. These addresses are checked during the search and go into the optimization list automatically. Do not add sites that already open: optimization will not help them and in rare cases may get in the way. If a site stopped opening after being added, remove it from the list. Router addresses have an “important” mark: without such a site the search on the router counts as failed. Exclusions are sites that optimization leaves alone: on this computer it is the “Exclusions” list (a site also gets there from Home via “Site does not open?”), on the router — the “On router” switch. If a site, such as a bank, broke after optimization was turned on, add it to exclusions.
info.domain_lists.title: Domain lists
info.domain_lists:
Nothing to do here: the lists update by themselves; your own sites go on the “Sites” tab.

Optimization is applied not to the whole internet but only to sites from the lists — this way it does not disturb anything else. The standard lists (YouTube, Discord and other sites that are hard to reach for many people) come with updates and cannot be edited. Add your own sites on the “Sites” tab. Exclusions — sites that optimization leaves alone: on this PC — “Sites” → “Exclusions”, on the router — “Sites” → “On router”. Subdomains are covered automatically: example.com also covers video.example.com.
info.ip_lists.title: IP lists
info.ip_lists:
Turn on “Lists only” if games or voice apps do not work; sites do not need it.

Some programs and games do not say which site they connect to — only the address (IP). For them optimization is turned on by a list of addresses of large networks (Cloudflare, Google, gaming and hosting companies). “Lists only” is needed for games, voice apps and sites that are slowed down entirely; YouTube and Discord do not need it. “Check whether optimization helps” turns optimization on for every connection for 10 minutes without checks — only to quickly see whether it helps at all: many sites misbehave meanwhile, so the mode turns itself off. The list updates together with the app data; your own subnets and exclusions can be added below.
info.game.title: Game mode
info.game:
Turn it on only if a game does not connect to its servers or in-game voice chat does not work.

Games use random ports rather than “web” ports, so regular optimization does not see them. Game mode turns optimization on for all those ports, but only towards addresses from the IP list, and adds a “decoy” to the first packets of each connection. Turn it on if a game does not connect to its servers or voice chat does not work — and even less so without optimization. Do not turn it on “just in case”: CPU load grows (especially with torrents), latency (ping) may increase, and some programs (VPN, remote desktop) may start to misbehave. Games with anti-cheat (for example, Vanguard, FACEIT, Easy Anti-Cheat) may refuse to start or let you into a match while the optimization driver (WinDivert) is running: better turn optimization off before such a game. If things got worse after turning it on, just turn it off.
info.apps.title: Games & apps — set up for a game
info.apps:
Use it if a game or program does not connect or stops after login while sites work.

“Set up for a game” records where the game connects while you launch it: addresses and ports, without traffic contents. System services, browsers and the local network are filtered out; the rest becomes a profile: optimization is turned on only for those addresses and ports, everything else stays as is. If it still does not work, the app tries other parameters (up to 5 attempts) and in the end restores everything as it was. Recording runs until you press “Done” and stops by itself after 5 minutes. Recording UDP needs the WinDivert driver (read-only): games with anti-cheat (Vanguard, FACEIT, Easy Anti-Cheat) may refuse to start or let you into a match. It does not help in every case: if the game server is unreachable for another reason, the profile changes nothing. “Restore” removes the profile.
info.debug.title: Connection debugging
info.debug:
Open it if “Set up for a game” did not help or the connections need to be chosen by hand.

All recorded connections are shown here: program, address, port, type (TCP or UDP) and, for TCP, state. The default marks are the same as in the simple mode; “Cut noise” restores them. A profile can be saved with any marks; parameters come from ready-made strategies — no commands need to be typed. UDP is recorded only with the WinDivert driver, without it — only TCP. In games where players connect directly (voice, matches) addresses are random: such a profile is helped by ports rather than addresses. The section is visible when “Show advanced tools” is on in “Settings” → “Advanced tools”.
info.hosts.title: hosts — “Fix addresses”
info.hosts:
Turn it on if files from GitHub do not download, Telegram Web does not open or Discord takes minutes to start.

Sometimes it is not the whole site that fails but one specific server address — then neither optimization nor another DNS helps, but the site has other addresses. The app can write such addresses into the system hosts file (a “site → address” list that Windows reads before DNS) — only for GitHub, Telegram and Discord and only after checking that the address really belongs to that site and responds. The entries are marked with a “DpiShell” block, other lines of the file stay unchanged; a copy of the file is kept, and “Restore” removes only DpiShell's lines. Windows Defender or another antivirus may warn about the hosts change — this is a reaction to any edit of that file (the button name in the warning depends on the version). Outdated addresses are checked once a day and removed automatically.
info.hosts_try.title: hosts — try lines
info.hosts_try:
Paste lines from a guide if you are not sure they are safe: try them first, write them after.

For each “address name” line the app checks whether the address responds and belongs to that site (certificate), whose address it is and whether the site opens via your DNS. “Helps” — the line fixes it; “Not needed” — the site opens anyway; “Breaks” — the site stops opening with it; “Dangerous” — the address does not belong to the site; “Won't help” — optimization is needed, not hosts; “Blocks” — the line simply closes the site. Only “Helps” lines can be written: into a separate “DpiShell user” block, each line marked dpishell-user. A copy of the file is kept, and “Restore” removes only DpiShell's lines. Site addresses change over time: once a day the app checks what was written and reports when an address stops working — it does not remove it by itself. “Check my hosts” analyzes other lines of the file the same way; they can be commented out only by your choice, nothing is deleted.
info.dns.title: DNS
info.dns:
Change DNS if “Check DNS” found spoofing; in a work network, leave it alone.

DNS turns a site name into an address. Some providers spoof the answers: the site “does not exist” although it does; browsers with their own secure DNS may cope by themselves, programs (Discord, games) cannot. “Check DNS” compares the answers of your DNS with a secure one (DoH — queries are encrypted, the provider does not see them and usually does not spoof them, but may block the secure DNS itself). If answers are spoofed, choose a secure DNS in “DNS of this computer” — the app changes it for Ethernet and Wi-Fi, and “Restore” brings back the values from before DpiShell (if you changed them yourself later, those edits may be overwritten). Do not turn it on if the computer is in a work network with internal addresses or you use router filters: they will stop working. DNS does not help when the server address itself is unreachable — that is what “Fix addresses” is for.
info.proxy.title: Proxy
info.proxy:
Set it up if you have your own proxy (for example, Clash) and programs should go through it; if no proxy is needed, keep the system proxy off.

The system proxy is the address Windows programs usually send connections through. “For this user” changes without administrator rights; “Via helper” and “For the whole machine” are done by the helper: for the machine the settings become shared by all users, and a checkbox also sets the proxy for Windows services (WinHTTP). Edge and Chrome usually use the system proxy, Firefox — whatever is set in it; programs with their own proxy, Microsoft Store apps (they may need a 127.0.0.1 exemption) and Windows services may not use it. “Turn proxy off” turns the system proxy off and remembers the previous one, “Restore previous” puts it back. “Check proxy” opens a connection to two sites through it and shows whether it responds. If the setting is enforced by an organization policy, changes may not apply. All changes go into “Undo all” in “DpiShell changes”.
info.diag.title: Diagnostics
info.diag:
Come here if optimization is on but sites do not open.

Here the app checks what interferes with optimization on this computer: similar programs (they need to be stopped), VPN, antivirus and “gaming” network services, proxy settings, extra lines in hosts. Come here if optimization is on but sites do not open, or before reporting a problem. Nothing changes until a button is pressed: each finding says what to do. Attach the file from “Save report” to a problem report — personal data is hidden in it. What interferes with optimization on the router is on the “Router” tab.
info.router_mode.title: Router — which sites are optimized
info.router_mode:
Keep “All sites”; choose “Lists only” if many sites break with it.

“All sites” — optimization for any site except exclusions: this way even sites missing from the lists open. If some site broke after that, enter it in “Site does not open” — the router checks it and offers to add it to exclusions. “Lists only” — optimization only for YouTube, Discord and sites from the lists; choose it if many sites break in “All sites” mode. After the mode changes, the router re-checks by itself that everything opens.
info.site_check.title: Site does not open
info.site_check:
Enter a site that stopped opening through the router — the router tells whether optimization gets in its way.

Enter the address of a site that does not open — the router checks it twice: with optimization and without. Opens only without optimization — optimization gets in its way: press “Add to exclusions” and the router leaves it alone. Opens with optimization — optimization is not the cause: reload the page or try another browser. Does not open even without optimization — the site itself is down or unreachable at that address.
info.router_dns.title: DNS for the whole network
info.router_dns:
Turn it on if the provider spoofs site addresses; not needed with the provider's parental control.

The router usually hands out DNS to every device at home: phones, TV, computers. If the provider spoofs answers, programs (Discord, games) get wrong addresses and optimization cannot help them. Secure DNS — the router looks addresses up via encrypted servers (DoH): the provider usually does not spoof them but may block the secure DNS itself. Do not turn it on if you use the provider's filters (parental control): they will stop working. The previous settings are kept, and “Restore” brings them back; your own later edits may be overwritten.
info.router_watchdog.title: Watchdog on the router
info.router_watchdog:
Keep it on: if optimization on the router breaks the internet, the router usually turns it off by itself.

Every few minutes the watchdog checks regular sites. If they do not open with optimization but open without it, the router turns optimization off and reports it here and on Home; then it runs one strategy search by itself, and if nothing is found, optimization stays off until you turn it on or start a search. The watchdog may miss breakage on other sites. Turn the watchdog off only if it triggers for no reason. Without the app: on most OpenWrt routers pressing reset for 2 seconds turns optimization off without a reboot, but yours may behave differently. Do not hold reset for 5 seconds or longer — that usually resets the router to factory settings.
info.advanced.title: Advanced mode — sites with their own strategy
info.advanced:
Turn it on if one site needs a different strategy than the rest; usually not required.

Off — everything works as usual, the lines are kept. On — the listed sites get their own strategy, and other sites work as chosen below. “Auto” — the search picks the strategy for the line, until then the current one is used. “Direct” in a line — optimization leaves those sites alone, but only while these settings are on; permanent router exclusions are in the “Exclusions” field under “Sites” → “On router”. Your lines take precedence over the YouTube and Discord lists: if you enter youtube.com, it follows your line. “Other sites”: “Lists only” — as usual; “All sites” may interfere with regular sites — on this computer it turns on only while optimization works and after regular sites are checked: if they stop opening, “Lists only” comes back; “Direct — no optimization” — only your lines work. Changes are saved with the “Save” button at the bottom of the tab; “Restore” brings back the previous lines. The search checks the first site of each line, so the result in your network cannot be guaranteed.
info.joint.title: Joint mode with the router
info.joint:
Turn it on if DpiShell runs both on the router and on this computer and your own sites need to be handled here; otherwise not needed.

The router optimizes YouTube and Discord itself, including for this computer, and the computer takes only your sites: “My sites” and lines from “Per-site settings”. Each address has one owner: a line that matches a router address (for example, youtube.com) is not applied on the computer — it is marked “handled by router”. Works only when DpiShell is on both the computer and the router and optimization is on at the router. If the router disappears or does not accept the link, the computer immediately works on its own, as before. The link renews itself; “Undo all” and “Remove optimization service” remove it. Off by default.
info.service.title: Service — working without the window
info.service:
Keeping the service is recommended: optimization works independently of the window.

The service is the background part of the app. With it, optimization keeps working after the app is closed and starts when Windows starts, even before you sign in.

Without the service, optimization works while the app is running — in the window or minimized to the tray (the icon next to the clock). Closing the app turns it off. After a restart it comes back only if “Start with Windows” is on, and only after you sign in.

Switching does not interrupt running optimization. To remove the service — “Settings” → “Remove optimization service”; to work without the service — “Settings” → “Service mode”.
info.av_exclusion.title: Defender exclusion: core folder
info.av_exclusion:
Add it if Defender deletes the zapret core: without the core, optimization does not work.

Defender sometimes flags the WinDivert driver from the zapret core: it intercepts network traffic, as malware does. The button adds one folder to the exclusions, %ProgramData%\DpiShell, where the core and the helper live; Defender stops scanning it. DpiShell does not exclude the folder the program was unpacked to: any program without administrator rights can write there, and an exclusion would turn it into a hiding place. It is added only when pressed; "Undo all" and removing DpiShell remove only this exclusion. For another antivirus, add the exclusion in its settings manually.
info.driver_block.title: Interception driver did not start
info.driver_block:
The interception driver (WinDivert) is required for optimization. Windows did not let it start - most often because of kernel protection: Windows Security > Device security > Core isolation.

- "Memory integrity" runs drivers in an isolated environment and allows only verified ones.
- "Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist" forbids drivers from a Microsoft list with known vulnerabilities. A separate switch exists on Windows 11 22H2 and later; on Windows 10 and earlier builds of 11 it may be missing - there the list works together with Memory integrity.

You can try turning off what is available in that section and restarting the PC. This lowers Windows protection: do it at your own risk, and only if you need to. You can turn it back on in the same place. Sometimes the cause is different - an antivirus or an organization policy; then the setting will not help.
